prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words, policy-focused, no names)

EU and constitutional
- Remain in the EU by revoking Article 50 if winning a majority; otherwise back a referendum with a remain option. Protect freedom of movement; extend national voting rights to EU citizens resident 5+ years. Use a projected £50bn “Remain Bonus” to fund services.
- Electoral reform to proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, automatic voter registration, overseas constituencies, and House of Lords reform. Stronger transparency for political ads and lobbying; citizens’ assemblies on major issues.
- Devolution: a written federal constitution; more powers and funding for nations, regions and local authorities; English devolution by consent.

Economy, work, business and tax
- £130bn infrastructure plan: transport (rail electrification, HS2/NPR support), schools, hospitals, housing (300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 social), fibre broadband, Green Investment Bank (£5bn).
- Regional Rebalancing Programme (£50bn) and Just Transition Fund; strengthen British Business Bank; local banking; support tourism.
- R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapults; skills strategy and high-quality apprenticeships; creative and tech sector support, AI ethics “Lovelace Code.”
- Small business support (start-up allowance, prompt payment enforcement); social enterprises; Future High Streets Fund.
- Modernise work: “dependent contractor” status, day-one flexible working, stronger enforcement, zero-hours protections, portable pensions, union access.
- Skills Wallets: £10,000 per adult over life for approved training.
- Tax: restore corporation tax to 20%; align taxation of income and capital; replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tougher action on multinational avoidance and digital taxation.

Education and childcare
- Free, high-quality childcare from 9 months for working parents (35 hours, 48 weeks); expand Children’s Centres; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; clear repairs backlog; enhanced SEND funding; teacher pay uplift and funded CPD.
- Replace SATs with moderated assessment; broader school performance measures; replace Ofsted with a new inspectorate; protect arts; “curriculum for life.”
- FE funding boost; maintenance grants restored; stronger student mental health; review HE finance.

Climate, environment, transport and animal welfare
- Net zero by 2045; at least 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking; £6bn+/year for a decade to insulate buildings; zero-carbon homes standard; heat decarbonisation.
- Nature Act with binding targets; plant 60m trees/year; major habitat restoration; circular economy law (single-use plastics bans, right to repair, deposit return, 70% recycling target).
- Transport: Clean Air Act; EV-only new car/van sales by 2030; rapid charging rollout; extend ULEZs; shift freight to rail; invest £4.5bn in buses; national walking/cycling strategy; rail fare freeze for commuters; reform franchising; new Railways Agency.
- Animal welfare: sentience in law; higher cruelty penalties; farm standards; phase out cages; tighter pet/fur rules.

Health, care, public health
- Additional £7bn/year via 1p on income tax for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; long-term Health and Care Tax after consultation; integrate health and social care.
- Mental health: new waiting-time standards; expand talking therapies; 24/7 crisis care in all hospitals; perinatal support; modernise Mental Health Act; end detention of people with learning disability/autism in ATUs.
- Workforce strategy; expand primary/community care; support carers (statutory respite, higher Carer’s Allowance earnings limit).
- Public health: National Wellbeing Strategy; stronger obesity, tobacco and alcohol measures; clean air right; evidence-led drug policy including a regulated cannabis market; decriminalise abortion and introduce safe access zones; PrEP access.

Social security, housing and communities
- Reform Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; remove two-child limit and benefits cap; higher work allowances; separate employment support; end WCAs; reinstate Independent Living Fund; legal right to food; LHA aligned to local rents; abolish bedroom tax; end fuel poverty by 2025.
- Pensions: retain triple lock; address issues affecting 1950s-born women.
- Housing: 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 social; zero-carbon standards; Rent to Own for social housing; longer private tenancies; rogue landlord licensing; measures on second homes/overseas buyers.
- End rough sleeping in five years: “somewhere safe to stay” duty; fund councils; scrap Vagrancy Act.
- Rural/coastal: £2bn Rural Services Fund; expand buses, broadband and mobile; coastal change fund.

Policing and justice
- £1bn for community policing; public health approach to violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; end disproportionate stop-and-search; replace PCCs with Police Boards; maintain EU crime cooperation tools.
- Justice: recruit 2,000 prison officers; presumption against short sentences; decriminalise drug possession for personal use; restorative justice; Women’s Justice Board; reduce ethnic disparities; better resettlement.

Rights, immigration and asylum
- Protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore legal aid (£500m); halt police facial recognition; no-fault divorce; cohabitation rights; gender recognition reform; X passports; BSL Act; free period products; accessibility.
- Immigration: end hostile environment; 28-day detention limit; move visa policy to relevant departments; merit-based work visas; two-year post-study work; reduce child citizenship fees; scrap spouse income rule; armed forces fee waivers; regularise long-resident children.
- Asylum: right to work after 3 months; resettle 10,000 refugees/year and 10,000 unaccompanied children over a decade; expand family reunion; move policymaking to development department; free English lessons; longer move-on period; healthcare access.

Foreign policy and defence
- Support multilateralism (UN, NATO); spend 0.7% GNI on aid with climate/gender focus; Magnitsky-style sanctions; suspend arms sales to Saudi Arabia; recognise Palestine; uphold Hong Kong commitments.
- Defence: spend 2% of GDP; cyber investment; three-boat nuclear deterrent at reduced readiness; improve forces housing and veterans’ support.
- Global climate leadership: strengthen Paris goals, push EU net-zero target, plastics treaty, biodiversity/oceans protection, end fossil subsidies worldwide.
